subject: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance
thread_body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@northstarbank.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Tomás Alvarez <tomas.alvarez@northstarbank.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance

Asha, Tomás —

Following up on your request for safer model/runtime updates on your Dedicated reserved pool.

We’re starting a limited beta of “Dedicated staged rollouts” (phased traffic shifting + gates + approvals + audit trail). We’d like to include Northstar as one of the first 2–3 enterprise tenants, if you’re still interested.

What we need to align on to proceed:
1) Beta window + scope
- Target start: week of Feb 10 (we can adjust for your change freeze)
- Scope: one Dedicated pool + one primary route/model to start

2) Success criteria (what “good” looks like)
- Example: 5% → 25% → 100% rollout with no SLO breach
- Gate set: p95 latency, 5xx rate, timeouts, queue depth, GPU utilization (defaults are configurable)

3) Governance / change management
- Who at Northstar can approve stage advances / abort
- Whether you want “manual approval required” at each stage vs auto-advance after a stable window
- Audit log expectations (you raised this in SUP-3981)

I attached a short overview PDF. If you can share your preferred approvers + any hard requirements for audit events/retention, we can send the beta enablement plan.

Attachment: Dedicated_Staged_Rollouts_Beta_Overview.pdf

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference


---

From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@northstarbank.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tomás Alvarez <tomas.alvarez@northstarbank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@northstarbank.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance

Lauren — yes, still interested.

A few requirements from our side:
- Manual approval required before any stage >5% (we can consider auto-advance later)
- Named approvers: myself + Tomás (SRE), with a break-glass abort path for our on-call
- Audit: we need an exportable record of approvals/aborts (actor, timestamp, what changed). Emily is looping in to validate this meets our change mgmt controls.

Change freeze note: We have a soft freeze Feb 24–Mar 7. If we can start the week of Feb 10 and finish before Feb 24, that would be ideal.

Can you share:
1) Whether the staged rollout can be limited to a single route/model and not affect our other routes on the pool
2) How rollback works if the gates fail (automatic vs manual)
3) The exact metrics you’ll gate on by default, and how missing metrics are handled

Thanks,
Asha

Asha Rao
Director, Platform Engineering
Northstar Bank


---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@northstarbank.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tomás Alvarez <tomas.alvarez@northstarbank.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@northstarbank.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 8:05 AM PST
Subject: Re: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance

Asha —

Thanks, that’s all consistent with how we’re running the beta.

High-level answers:
1) Scoped rollout
Yes — we can scope the staged rollout to a single route (or a small set) on your Dedicated pool. Other routes stay on the current pinned version.

2) Rollback behavior
In beta, the default behavior on gate failure is “auto-hold” (pause progression) + notify. You can then choose to abort (rollback) or proceed after investigation.
If you prefer, we can configure “auto-abort” for specific severe gate failures (e.g., 5xx > X%) but we typically keep this manual for enterprise until we see stable behavior.

3) Default gates + missing metrics
Default gates (proposed):
- p95 latency (per-route)
- 5xx rate
- timeout rate
- queue depth
- pool GPU utilization

Missing/late metrics: the system will fail-safe into HOLD (i.e., it will not proceed). We’ll also surface “metrics stale” as the reason so your on-call isn’t guessing.

Lauren will follow with a proposed success criteria worksheet + a suggested 3-stage plan that fits your Feb 10–Feb 24 window.

Rachel

Rachel Kim
Enterprise Customer Success
Redwood Inference


---

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@northstarbank.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@northstarbank.com>, Tomás Alvarez <tomas.alvarez@northstarbank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 10:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance

Hi Lauren,

From a controls perspective, we need to confirm the audit trail covers:
- Create/update rollout plan
- Stage approval (who approved which stage)
- Abort/rollback
- System-initiated holds (with reason / failed gate)

Also:
- Retention: minimum 1 year accessible, 7 years archived is preferred (we can accept 1 year in-product if you support export)
- Access control: approver/abort permissions should be restricted to named roles. If there’s a “break-glass” mechanism, it must be logged.

If you have a sample audit event format (even if it’s not finalized), please share.

Thank you,
Emily

Emily Chen
GRC / Security Controls
Northstar Bank

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@northstarbank.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@northstarbank.com>, Tomás Alvarez <tomas.alvarez@northstarbank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance

Emily —

Jumping in from Security.

We will cover the audit event types you listed (create/update/approve/abort/system-hold). For each event, the fields include:
- actor (user/service), actor_type
- tenant_id, pool_id
- rollout_plan_id, plan_version, stage_id (if applicable)
- action (e.g., rollout.stage.approve)
- timestamp
- diff/summary of change (for create/update)
- result + reason (for holds)

Retention/export:
- In-product audit log view: 13 months (current enterprise default)
- Export: supported via our audit log export pipeline (SIEM-friendly). For beta we can enable export to your preferred sink if you already have an integration, or provide periodic exports.

Access control:
- Approve/abort are gated by explicit permissions (separate from “edit”).
- “Break-glass” is supported only for Redwood on-call during beta; it’s audited and requires an incident reference.

If you’re comfortable, I can send a redacted sample payload as plain text in email.

Marcus

Marcus Lin
Security Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@northstarbank.com>, Tomás Alvarez <tomas.alvarez@northstarbank.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@northstarbank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance

Asha/Tomás —

Proposing a beta plan that fits your timing and keeps blast radius small:

Rollout target
- Pool: northstar-prod-dedicated-us-east-1 (your current reserved pool)
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (one model alias only)
- Change: model version bump + runtime config (KV cache tuning) under a new rollout plan

Stages (manual approvals)
- Stage 0: internal shadow (0% customer traffic; Redwood verification)
- Stage 1: 5% for 30 min stable window (manual approve to enter; manual approve to leave)
- Stage 2: 25% for 60 min stable window (manual approve)
- Stage 3: 100%

Proposed default gates (Stage 1+)
- p95 latency: no worse than +10% vs baseline over evaluation window
- 5xx rate: <= 0.2%
- timeout rate: <= 0.1%
- queue depth: <= baseline + fixed headroom threshold
- GPU utilization: <= 85% sustained (to prevent saturation)

Success criteria (draft)
1) At least one full staged rollout completed with no SLO breach and no manual intervention beyond approvals
2) At least one “negative test” (intentionally low threshold in staging or during Stage 1) triggers HOLD and produces clear UI + audit event
3) Approver workflow + audit export validated by Emily’s team

I attached a worksheet with the above so you can edit thresholds/windows.

Attachment: Northstar_Beta_Success_Criteria_Worksheet.xlsx

If you confirm the approvers list + your preferred meeting time, we’ll schedule a 45-min kickoff to finalize thresholds and the change window.

Lauren

From: Tomás Alvarez <tomas.alvarez@northstarbank.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@northstarbank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@northstarbank.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 20, 2025 at 2:33 PM PST
Subject: Re: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance

Lauren —

This looks workable.

A couple SRE notes:
- For Stage 1, can we shorten the evaluation window to 15 min? Our traffic is spiky and we’d like to keep the canary small-timeboxed.
- We’d like the ability to “hold” indefinitely without the system auto-advancing if someone forgets to approve.
- On abort, do you revert traffic instantly to the prior version, or do you drain? We need to understand if there’s a period of mixed versions.

Approvers: Asha + me.

Kickoff times that work this week (PT):
- Tue 1–3pm
- Wed 9–11am

Tomás

Tomás Alvarez
SRE Manager
Northstar Bank

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tomás Alvarez <tomas.alvarez@northstarbank.com>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@northstarbank.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@northstarbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 23, 2025 at 4:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Beta participation: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — success criteria + governance

Tomás —

All good asks.

- Stage 1 window: yes, we can do 15 min as long as we keep a minimum datapoint count (we’ll set a floor so the gate doesn’t evaluate on near-zero traffic).
- Manual holds: confirmed — in beta, stage advancement is never automatic when “manual approvals required” is enabled. It will remain in HOLD until an approver advances or aborts.
- Abort semantics: traffic allocation flips back to the prior pinned version immediately at the router policy level. In-flight requests finish on the version they started with; there can be a brief period where both versions are serving due to in-flight work, but new requests go entirely to the prior version.

Next step: let’s do Wed 9:30–10:15am PT. Invite coming from Rachel.

For Emily: Marcus will bring sample audit events + retention/export details to the kickoff so we can close out the controls questions.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
